pattern_name: Phrasal verbs, collocations and register — B2 review
pattern_name_ar: الأفعال المركبة والمتلازمات والمقام — مراجعة B2
formula: separable: verb + object + particle (pronoun MUST go in the middle) · inseparable: verb + particle + object · phrasal (informal) vs Latinate (formal) equivalents
formula_visual: [turn it off] ✅ // [turn off it] ❌ // [put off] = informal, [postpone] = formal
when_to_use: Separable phrasal verbs allow 'turn off the light' or 'turn the light off', but with a PRONOUN the particle must follow it: 'turn it off'. Inseparable verbs never split: 'look after him'. Choose phrasal verbs for conversation and their one-word Latinate equivalents (postpone, discover, investigate) for formal contexts.
when_to_use_ar: الأفعال القابلة للفصل تسمح بالترتيبين، لكن مع الضمير يأتي حرف الجر بعده: 'turn it off'. وغير القابلة للفصل لا تنفصل. واختر المركّب للمحادثة والرسمي للمقامات الرسمية.
why_arabic_speakers_struggle: Arabic verbs don't split, so 'turn off it' feels natural. Learners also treat phrasal verbs as informal-only and avoid them in speech (sounding stiff), or use them in formal writing (sounding too casual). Register control is the final B2 skill.

examples.en: Could you turn it off, please?
Turn off the light. / Turn the light off.
examples.structure: [separable, both orders OK with a noun]

examples.en: We had to put off the meeting. / The meeting was postponed.

common_errors.explanation: With a pronoun the particle must come after it.
'look after' is inseparable and never splits.

common_errors.wrong: The committee will look into the matter. (in a formal report)
common_errors.correct: The committee will investigate the matter.
common_errors.explanation: Formal writing prefers the one-word Latinate equivalent.

practice_fill_blank.sentence: I'll look ___ him while you're away.
We had to put ___ the meeting. (informal)
The meeting was ___ until March. (formal for 'put off')
She handed out the ___ . (noun from 'hand out')

quick_rule: Pronoun ALWAYS goes between verb and particle: 'turn it off'. Inseparable verbs never split. Phrasal = conversation, Latinate = formal.
quick_rule_ar: الضمير دائمًا بين الفعل وحرف الجر: 'turn it off'. وغير القابل للفصل لا ينفصل. المركّب للمحادثة والرسمي للمقام الرسمي.
mnemonic: Pronoun in the middle. Casual → phrasal · Formal → one word.
connect_to_speaking: In accent week 16 you drilled particle stress and register rhythm. Say 'put it OFF' (fast, casual) against 'postPONE it' (measured, formal). This completes B2 — you now control not just accuracy but appropriacy.
